messages.author: 4007f3a28f71aa25
messages.subject: Noob question about datasets
parts:
Hello,

I am learning R for the first time (will be taking a full fledged course in the Fall) to produce boxplots of remote sensing data. These are simple pairs of data where I classify the terrain as one of two types. The software I use outputs data in the format:

BIR_WATER     BIR_NOTWATER
0.45664            1.646
0.65412            2.456
etc.


If I use boxplot() function in R I get standard boxplots (quantile-based) without formatting my data differently. I need to produce standard deviation-based plots so this is how I found ggplot2. The problem is I cannot get it to work with the data organized as above. After reading a bit of documentation I re-arranged the data as:

BIR_WATER           0.45664
BIR_WATER           0.65412
BIR_WATER           etc.
BIR_NOTWATER     1.646
BIR_NOTWATER     2.456

and I can produce plots just fine using ggplot2 by declaring x as the first variable and y as the second.

Re-arranging the data to this format is not a problem, but I am sure I am missing something completely obvious. Not averse to being pointed to further documentation to figure it out instead of it being spelled out for me ;)

Thanks for your time,
JF Prieur

messages.author: 4d07036acfc68466
messages.subject: Re: Noob question about datasets
parts:
Hi JF Prieur,

Many functions in R expect data to be in a long format rather than a wide format as in SPSS.

Here's information I used to find about this issue on the cookbook for R website:
http://www.cookbook-r.com/Manipulating_data/Converting_data_between_wide_and_long_format/

Hope it helps. :)
Xi
